name: Mount Washington via Tuckerman Ravine
region: White Mountain National Forest, New Hampshire
why: Up the bowl of Tuckerman Ravine and its headwall to the top of New England, the summit with the worst recorded weather on Earth.
book: No permit. Pinkham Notch Visitor Center (AMC) at the trailhead. The summit has a state park building, food and the Cog Railway and Auto Road down if needed.
water: Water at Hermit Lake; drinking water at the summit building in summer.
dangers: Weather turns in minutes: fog, hurricane-force wind and snow even in summer. More than 160 people have died on the mountain.
The headwall is steep with loose rock; closed when there is snow and ice.
Spring avalanches in the ravine until June.
turnaround: Turn at Lunch Rocks or Hermit Lake if the summit is in cloud and wind is rising.
